neighbours.label: predicting a young child's age (5 or 4) next: 'when they turn' in a child or school context
fire: Kids in our district may enter kindergarten once they turn 5 before September.
Parents often ask whether a boy who turns 5 in August is ready for school.
The preschool accepts toddlers until they turn 4 and then moves them up.
My niece starts school next year, right after she turns 5 in the spring.
Most kindergarten classes are full of children who just turned 5 that summer.
Our son was still in daycare when he turned 4 last winter.
In many countries a child begins reception class after turning 5.
Teachers notice that pupils who turn 5 just before the cut-off are often younger in class.
quiet: Workers in our district may retire once they turn 65 before September.
Parents often ask whether a teenager who turns 16 in August is ready to drive.
The club accepts members until they turn 30 and then moves them up.
My uncle starts his pension next year, right after he turns 67 in the spring.
Most graduate classes are full of students who just turned 23 that summer.
Our grandfather was still farming when he turned 80 last winter.
In many countries a citizen may vote after turning 18.
Coaches notice that players who turn 30 just before the season are often slower.
